extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners and patent practitioners prosecuting U.S. national applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on restriction (election/division) practice and double patenting rejections under 35 U.S.C. 121 and related rules for national (35 U.S.C. 111) patent applications, including special handling (Markush, nucleotide sequences, transitional applications) and rejoinder. Primarily directed at examiners but also relevant to applicants and practitioners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory and regulatory basis for restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: The basis for restriction and double patenting practices is found in 35 U.S.C. 121 and 37 CFR 1.141–1.142, which provide that if two or more independent and distinct inventions are claimed in one application, the Director may require restriction to one invention and the examiner shall require the applicant to elect the invention to which the claims will be restricted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quotes of the statutes and rules are provided (35 U.S.C. 121; 37 CFR 1.141(a), 1.142(a)–(b)). The rule permits more than one species in one application only where a generic claim is allowable and excess species are in dependent form or include all limitations of the generic claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'independent'
rubrics_metrics.description: 'Independent' means not dependent, or unrelated — there is no disclosed relationship between the two or more inventions claimed (i.e., they are unconnected in design, operation, and effect).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: a process and an apparatus incapable of being used in practicing the process are independent. See MPEP §§ 802.01, 806.06, 808.01 for additional examples.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of 'related but distinct' (distinctness test)
rubrics_metrics.description: Related inventions are disclosed as connected in design, operation, or effect (e.g., combination and subcombination, process and apparatus, process and product). Related inventions are 'distinct' if the inventions as claimed are not connected in at least one of design, operation, or effect (e.g., can be made by, or used in, a materially different process) and wherein at least one invention is PATENTABLE (novel and nonobvious) OVER THE OTHER.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A two-way test is required for some relation types (see MPEP § 806.05(c) and § 806.05(j)). Even if each is unpatentable over the prior art, distinctness exists if one is patentable over the other. Read decisions carefully because 'independent' and 'distinct' have varied meanings in case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of restriction (practical)
rubrics_metrics.description: Restriction is the practice of requiring an applicant to elect a single claimed invention (e.g., a combination or subcombination, a product or process, a species within a genus) for examination when independent and/or two or more distinct inventions are claimed in an application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Restriction results in non-elected claims being withdrawn from consideration (37 CFR 1.142(b)) unless reinstated if the requirement is withdrawn or overruled.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two criteria for a proper requirement for restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: There are two criteria for a proper requirement for restriction between patentably distinct inventions: (A) The inventions must be independent or distinct as claimed; and (B) There would be a serious burden on the examiner if restriction is not required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both criteria must be satisfied to support a restriction. Where plural inventions can be viewed as related in two ways, both applicable criteria must be demonstrated. Examiners must provide reasons and/or examples to support conclusions (though citation of documents is not required in most cases).

rubrics_metrics.name: Serious burden prima facie showing
rubrics_metrics.description: For purposes of the initial requirement, a serious burden on the examiner may be prima facie shown by appropriate explanation of separate classification, separate status in the art, or a different field of search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The prima facie showing may be rebutted by applicant evidence/argument. See MPEP § 808.02 for field-of-search related guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: When restriction is improper (obviousness between inventions)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there is an express admission that the claimed inventions would have been obvious over each other within the meaning of 35 U.S.C. 103, restriction should not be required (In re Lee).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Case law requires not restricting where inventions are essentially the same for obviousness purposes. Examiners should check for admissions or evidence of obviousness between claimed inventions before issuing a restriction requirement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiner signatory authority for final restriction requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Only an examiner with permanent full signatory authority or temporary full signatory authority may sign final Office actions containing a final requirement for restriction; examiners with partial signatory authority may sign non-final Office actions containing a final requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This measure guards against issuance of improper requirements that might lead to duplicate patents for the same invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Markush group membership requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of a Markush group ordinarily must belong to a recognized physical or chemical class or to an art-recognized class. For Markush groups in process or combination claims (not single compounds), it is sufficient that the members are disclosed to possess at least one property in common mainly responsible for their function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Markush claims are common in chemistry/biology but can also be used for mechanical features or process steps. The examiner should assess whether enumeration groups are class-recognized or share a property essential to the claimed function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unity test for Markush-type claims
rubrics_metrics.description: Unity of invention exists where compounds included within a Markush group (1) share a common utility, and (2) share a substantial structural feature essential to that utility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If Markush members meet unity, the claim should be examined as a whole; otherwise treatment as encompassing independent/distinct inventions (and provisional election) may be appropriate. See In re Weber, In re Haas, In re Harnisch, Ex parte Hozumi decisions cited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine all Markush members when no serious burden
rubrics_metrics.description: If the members of the Markush group are sufficiently few in number or so closely related that a search and examination of the entire claim can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine all the members of the Markush group in the claim on the merits, even though they may be directed to independent and distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In such cases the examiner will not require provisional election or provisional election procedures. See MPEP § 808.02.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional election procedure for Markush claims
rubrics_metrics.description: In applications containing a Markush-type claim that encompasses at least two independent or distinct inventions, the examiner may require a provisional election of a single species prior to examination on the merits. The elected species will be examined fully; the Markush claim will be examined with respect to the elected species and to the extent necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the elected species is found unpatentable, the Markush claim and claims to the elected species are rejected and nonelected species are held withdrawn. If the elected species is allowable, examination of the Markush claim will be extended; prior art may lead to rejection of the Markush claim with nonelected species withdrawn. Examiners should use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., form paragraph 8.01 or 8.02) and follow procedures for making final actions and possible finality per MPEP § 706.07(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional application restriction rule (37 CFR 1.129)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications (other than reissue/design) pending at least three years as of June 8, 1995, no requirement for restriction or divisional filing shall be made or maintained after June 8, 1995, except where: (i) the requirement was first made prior to April 8, 1995; (ii) the examiner was prevented from making a requirement prior to April 8, 1995 due to applicant actions; or (iii) the required fee for examination of each additional invention was not paid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If restriction cannot be maintained under 1.129(b), applicant is notified and given options to elect and pay fees, confirm and pay, or file a petition. Form paragraph 8.41 may be used to notify applicants subject to transitional provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Actions by the applicant that can prevent restriction prior to April 8, 1995
rubrics_metrics.description: Examples include: (A) applicant abandoned the application and continued to refile so no Office action could be issued; (B) applicant requested suspension of prosecution under 37 CFR 1.103(a) preventing Office action; (C) applicant delayed presenting claims to more than one disclosed independent/distinct invention such that no restriction requirement could be made prior to April 8, 1995; (D) applicant combined several applications into one continuing application and delayed filing so no restriction requirement could be made prior to April 8, 1995.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an examiner believes the application falls under the exception because of applicant action, the application must be brought to the Technology Center Special Program Examiner for review. Extensions under 37 CFR 1.136(a) do not constitute such actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transitional application fee/payment and remedy
rubrics_metrics.description: If a transitional application contains more than one independent and distinct invention and a restriction cannot be maintained, applicant will be given time to: (i) elect the invention(s) to be searched and examined and pay the fee in 37 CFR 1.17(s) for each additional invention elected; (ii) confirm a prior election and pay the fee; or (iii) file a petition traversing the requirement. If fees for additional inventions are not paid, those inventions will be withdrawn from consideration and may be pursued in a divisional under 35 U.S.C. 121.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a timely petition defers the original time period for electing and paying the fee until decision on petition. No petition fee is required under 37 CFR 1.129(b)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Refunds when linking or generic claims become allowable (transitional)
rubrics_metrics.description: Whenever divided inventions in a transitional application are rejoined because a linking claim is allowable, or whenever claims to an additional species for which the fee was paid are fully embraced by an allowable generic claim, applicant should be notified that they may request a refund of the fee paid for that additional invention/species.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use form paragraphs and procedures referenced (MPEP § 803.03(a), § 803.03(b); MPEP § 821.04 and § 821.04(a)). Determination of when nonelected species are no longer withdrawn is made as indicated in MPEP § 806.04(d), § 821.04, and § 821.04(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Nucleotide sequence partial waiver (reasonable number rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Polynucleotide molecules encoding different proteins are normally independent and distinct inventions; however the Director has partially waived 37 CFR 1.141 et seq. to permit a reasonable number of such nucleotide sequences to be claimed in a single application—normally ten sequences constitute a reasonable number for examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most cases up to ten independent and distinct nucleotide sequences will be examined without restriction; sequences patentably indistinct from the selected sequences will also be examined. Sequences encoding the same protein are not considered independent and distinct and will be examined together. Exceptional cases may require fewer than ten. Applicants may petition under 37 CFR 1.181 for additional sequences with evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of claims to combinations of sequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications claiming only a combination of nucleotide sequences (e.g., a combination comprising SEQ ID Nos. 1-1000) will generally not be subject to restriction; presence of one novel and nonobvious sequence in the combination will render the entire combination allowable. Applications claiming combinations of different combinations will generally be subject to restriction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For combination claims, the examiner will search until one sequence is found to be allowable and may consider whether the combination as a whole renders the claim allowable if no individual sequence is allowable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rejoinder of process claims upon allowance of product claim
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims directed to a product and to a process of making and/or using the product are presented, if applicant elects the product and the product claim is subsequently found allowable, withdrawn process claims which depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable product claim will be considered for rejoinder and fully examined. All claims directed to a nonelected process invention must depend from or otherwise require all the limitations of an allowable product claim for rejoinder to occur.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If applicant cancels nonelected process claims before rejoinder, the examiner should not withdraw the restriction to preserve applicant’s rights under 35 U.S.C. 121. Applicants are encouraged to present process claims early and preferably as dependent claims to expedite rejoinder. Use appropriate form paragraphs (e.g., 8.42, 8.43). Amendments after allowance and after final rejection have different entry rules (37 CFR 1.312 and 1.116 respectively).

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on entry of amendments that would necessitate rejoinder raising new issues
rubrics_metrics.description: An amendment after final rejection that would place elected product claim(s) in condition for allowance and thereby require rejoinder of process claims that raise new issues (e.g., 35 U.S.C. 101 or 112 first paragraph issues) may be denied entry. For example, an amendment whose entry would necessitate further consideration of new statutory issues may be refused to avoid prejudice to prosecution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before mailing an advisory action in such situations, it is recommended to call applicant and give opportunity to cancel process claims or file an RCE. If in effect the final rejection is not sustainable and rejoined claims would be rejected, the examiner must issue a new Office action governed by MPEP § 706.07 regarding finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of conflicting claims in plural/copending applications (37 CFR 1.78)
rubrics_metrics.description: Where two or more applications filed by the same applicant contain conflicting claims, elimination of such claims from all but one application may be required in the absence of good and sufficient reason for their retention during pendency. When claims are patentably indistinct across copending applications, applicant must cancel them from all but one or maintain clear demarcation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A complete examination should be made of claims in each application and appropriate rejections (including provisional double patenting) should be entered in each application. The provisional double patenting rejection should continue in each application as long as conflicting claims exist unless it is the only remaining rejection in an application. Where appropriate, conflicting applications should be joined. Use form paragraphs (e.g., 8.29) where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional double patenting practice for copending applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Where claims in plural applications of the same inventive entity are unpatentable over claims of another application of the same inventive entity (or different inventive entity with common ownership), examiners may enter provisional statutory and/or nonstatutory double patenting rejections in each application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Such provisional double patenting rejections should remain unless it is the only rejection left in an application. See MPEP § 804.01 and § 822 for additional discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden of search/examination versus restriction
rubrics_metrics.description: If the search and examination of all the claims in an application can be made without serious burden, the examiner must examine them on the merits, even though they include claims to independent or distinct inventions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess burden objectively (see serious burden prima facie showing guidance). If burden is demonstrated, restriction may be proper; otherwise examine all claims.
